name: Gao & Wald 2000, Jacobi matrix equation (eq. 11): A'' = -T A, conjugate point at det A = 0

source.located: Gao & Wald, 'Theorems on gravitational time delay and related issues', CQG 17, 4999 (2000), arXiv gr-qc/0007021v2, p.7 eqs.(11)-(13). Eq.(11) as quoted verbatim from the full text: d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta (Wald's index convention); eq.(12) G = sqrt(det A); eq.(13) G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]. Independent restatement: Osorio Morales & Santillan, arXiv:2004.12523v4 (2022) sec.2.1 eq.(2.1) with the same initial data, 'q = gamma(lambda_0) is said to be conjugated to p if and only if det(A(lambda_0)) = 0', and 'det(A(lambda_0)) = 0 implies that there exist some initial conditions such that eta(q) = 0, thus q is a conjugate point to p in the usual sense' (p.5).

published_statement: Gao & Wald (2000) eq.(11): for a null geodesic from p with affine parameter lambda and tangent k, the Jacobi matrix obeys d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu with A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta -- i.e. the geodesic-deviation equation eta'' = -R(k, eta)k (Wald: a^c = -R_{abd}^c xi^b T^a T^d), equivalently on a transverse screen eta_i'' = -K_ij eta_j with K_ij = R_{k e_i k e_j} (MTW sign). A point q is conjugate to p where det A = 0 (restated in these words by 2004.12523 eq.(2.1)); eq.(13) G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma^2 + R_kk] with G = sqrt(det A) follows from the Raychaudhuri equation (quoted from ref.[10], FMW hep-th/9908070). Eq.(11) is a kinematic identity of Lorentzian geometry: it assumes no energy condition; Gao-Wald's Lemma 1/Theorem 1 add NEC + null generic condition only to GUARANTEE that a zero of det A occurs.
published_hypotheses: H1 null geodesic gamma, affinely parametrised, tangent k (2004.12523 adds the normalisation k.t = -1 against a global timelike t)
H2 congruence from a point: A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta (twist-free by construction, so eq.(13) carries no vorticity term)
H3 smooth (C^2) Lorentzian metric; no energy condition, no symmetry, no field equation is needed for eq.(11) itself

H4 four dimensions for the coefficient 1/2 in eq.(13) and for G = sqrt(det A) (sibling audit rederive A1-A3); det A of the literal 4x4 matrix equals lambda^2 det A_perp (sibling B2), so det A = 0 at lambda > 0 is det A_perp = 0
H5 sign convention of the curvature term: Wald's R_{abc}^d with the deviation equation's minus sign; any implementation must pair its Riemann convention with the matching sign

H6 (for the achronality consequence, not in eq.(11)) a null geodesic is not achronal past a point conjugate to p (Hawking-Ellis Prop. 4.5.12, NAMED-NOT-READ; used by Gao-Wald's J+(p) - I+(p) arguments)

later_literature.ref: Osorio Morales & Santillan, 'About apparent superluminal drives in generic gravity theories', arXiv:2004.12523v4 (2022)
later_literature.what: Restates Gao-Wald eq.(11) with A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta, the det A = 0 definition, and that det A = 0 yields a Jacobi field vanishing at both ends ('a conjugate point in the usual sense', p.5); extends the continuity lemma to generic gravity via the Raychaudhuri equation with sigma^2 retained. Their eq.(2.1) writes the curvature term as -R^mu_{alpha beta gamma} k^alpha k^beta A^gamma, a different index order from Gao-Wald's -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta -- a reminder that the sign of the tidal term is convention-laden across restatements, which is exactly where composite's implementation drifted.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for eq.(11): it has no empirical input. It is the geodesic-deviation (Jacobi) equation, a kinematic identity of any smooth Lorentzian metric, classical long before 2000 and restated unchanged in 2022 (2004.12523 eq.2.1); re-derived here symbolically (E1). There is no datum the authors could have lacked, and nothing measured since bears on it. Evidence the other way -- that something is wrong -- was sought and found only in the TREE's implementation: composite.py integrates the equation with the curvature term's sign reversed (E2, E3b). That is not missing data and not an error in Gao-Wald; for the vacuum rays composite actually uses it changes no number (E4), and it would change results only on rays through matter (E9).

The TREE's use is NARROWED, shown and not presumed: composite.py's implementation of eq.(11) (composite.py:233 T = -R_{k e_i k e_j}; :256 A'' = -T A) carries the curvature term with the opposite sign (E2), confirmed convention-free against the owner's own geodesic flow (E3b: axes swapped). It agrees with eq.(11) only on the class where the optical tidal matrix is traceless and diagonal (R_kk = 0, reflection-symmetric ray) -- a hypothesis the tree does not state. Every verdict resting on it lies inside that class and SURVIVES: the window table and 'SEATS AND EARLY' at M = -2e-3 are reproduced exactly with the sign corrected (E4b) and by an independent eq.(11) integration (E5: 56.56 vs 56.50; 55.21 vs 55.17); SR3's composite.survey(+2e-3) seats = True, delay > 0 is unchanged. Further named narrowings: the det-sign detector is sufficient, not necessary (E7); 'pure Weyl' holds to ~5 % where the field is weak (E5). Not WRONG: nothing in the source is contradicted, and no verdict that rests on it moves. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum.
